input.strategy_title: Queue-aware GPU scheduling for distributed training workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Large training jobs fail or waste capacity because pods are admitted piecemeal:
a 16-GPU job can hold 12 GPUs for hours waiting for the last 4, starving other
teams, and partially scheduled jobs die on timeout. Customers running mixed
fleets also report that jobs land on suboptimal GPU topologies (crossing NVLink
domains) with significant throughput loss. We need admission and placement that
treats a multi-node training job as one unit and uses GPU topology where it
matters.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Per-project GPU quota is enforced at admission time across training job types (PyTorchJob, RayJob). |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Users can see queue position, quota consumption, and admission state for their pending jobs in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Job placement can prefer GPU-topology-aligned nodes when the cluster exposes topology information. |

## Affected Components

- Distributed Workloads
- Training Operator
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- GPU sharing/fractioning (MIG, time-slicing policy management)
- Cross-cluster or multi-cluster queueing

## Open Questions

1. Do Kueue's current gang-admission semantics (waitForPodsReady) actually
   satisfy HLR-1 for PyTorchJob and RayJob at our target scale, or do we need
   scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue? The answer changes
   the shape of most implementation work.
2. Topology-aware placement (HLR-5) depends on node topology discovery that is
   only Tech Preview — is it mature enough to build on this release?
3. What preemption semantics do reference customers actually need — full
   eviction with requeue, or checkpoint-aware graceful preemption? We have
   conflicting field signals and no benchmark of checkpoint overhead.

# Enable Kueue-native gang admission for training workloads

## Description

Branch A of the gang-admission implementation (applies when the gang-admission
investigation concludes that Kueue's native semantics satisfy the
all-or-nothing requirement at target scale): enable and configure Kueue-native
gang admission so multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing, with
no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods.

## Scope

- Configure Kueue admission (waitForPodsReady semantics) for training
  workloads so a job's pods are admitted as a unit.
- Enable gang admission for RayJob workloads through the Kueue/KubeRay
  integration in the platform's midstream queueing components.
- Tune admission timeout/requeue behavior for partially schedulable jobs so
  they do not hold GPUs while waiting for remaining pods.
- Validate all-or-nothing admission for multi-node jobs under contention at
  the scale criteria established by the investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a 16-GPU job of which only 12 GPUs are currently available, when the
  job is submitted, then it remains fully pending and holds no GPUs.
- Given a multi-node RayJob and PyTorchJob under queue contention, when
  admitted, then all pods start together or the job is requeued.
- Given jobs that cannot be fully admitted within the configured timeout,
  when the timeout expires, then they are evicted/requeued without leaving
  partial GPU occupation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): multi-node training jobs admitted all-or-nothing, no partial
  GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods.

# Policy-driven Kueue preemption with eviction and requeue

## Description

Branch A of the preemption implementation (applies when the preemption
semantics investigation concludes that full eviction with requeue satisfies
customer needs): configure policy-driven preemption in the queueing layer so
higher-priority workloads preempt lower-priority ones according to an
admin-defined policy, with preempted jobs requeued rather than checkpointed.

## Scope

- Expose admin-defined preemption policy configuration (which workloads may
  preempt which, and requeue behavior) on the platform's queueing
  configuration.
- Ensure preempted jobs are evicted fully (no partial GPU occupation left
  behind) and requeued for later re-admission.
- Validate preemption behavior with mixed-priority training workloads
  (PyTorchJob and RayJob).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an admin-defined preemption policy, when a higher-priority workload
  is admitted, then lower-priority workloads are preempted per the policy.
- Given a preempted job, when eviction completes, then all its GPUs are
  released and the job is requeued (no partial occupation).
- Given a requeued preempted job, when capacity becomes available, then it
  is re-admitted and restarted.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones
  according to an admin-defined policy.

# Scheduler-plugin gang scheduling (coscheduling) for training workloads

## Description

Branch B of the gang-admission implementation (applies when the gang-admission
investigation concludes that Kueue's native semantics do NOT satisfy the
all-or-nothing requirement at target scale): implement gang scheduling for
training workloads (PyTorchJob and RayJob) via scheduler-plugin work
(e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue, so multi-node jobs are scheduled
all-or-nothing.

## Scope

- Design and integrate a scheduler-plugin gang scheduling capability (e.g.
  coscheduling pod groups) for the platform's training workloads, based on
  the failure evidence gathered by the investigation.
- Ensure RayJob workloads, through the Kueue/KubeRay integration in the
  platform's midstream queueing components, participate in the plugin's gang
  scheduling path alongside PyTorchJob.
- Wire the queueing layer's admission decisions to the plugin's gang
  scheduling semantics so admitted jobs are co-scheduled as units.
- Handle partial-schedulability: jobs that cannot be fully placed must not
  hold GPUs while waiting for remaining pods.
- Validate all-or-nothing scheduling at the scale criteria established by
  the investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a multi-node training job that cannot be fully placed, when the
  scheduler attempts placement, then no GPU is partially occupied by the
  job while it waits.
- Given sufficient capacity, when a multi-node RayJob or PyTorchJob is
  scheduled, then all pods start as a unit (gang).
- Given the plugin is active, when unrelated non-training workloads are
  scheduled, then default scheduling behavior is not regressed.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): multi-node training jobs admitted all-or-nothing, no partial
  GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods.

# Checkpoint-aware graceful preemption

## Description

Branch B of the preemption implementation (applies when the preemption
semantics investigation concludes that checkpoint-aware graceful preemption
is required): implement graceful preemption in the queueing layer so that
when a higher-priority workload preempts a running training job, the job's
progress is checkpointed before eviction and restored after requeue, per the
admin-defined policy.

## Scope

- Implement graceful preemption orchestration in the queueing layer:
  trigger a checkpoint before eviction, evict, requeue, and restore from the
  checkpoint on re-admission.
- Integrate with the training-job checkpoint capability (PyTorchJob
  checkpoint support) so progress is captured and restored for multi-node
  jobs.
- Make graceful versus plain eviction selectable through the admin-defined
  preemption policy.
- Validate checkpoint overhead in practice against the benchmark produced by
  the preemption semantics investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running training job is preempted under a graceful-preemption
  policy, when preemption occurs, then a checkpoint is taken before eviction
  and all GPUs are released.
- Given the preempted job is requeued and re-admitted, when it restarts, then
  it resumes from the checkpoint rather than starting from scratch.
- Given an admin-defined policy that selects plain eviction, when
  preemption occurs, then behavior matches full-eviction-with-requeue
  semantics.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones
  according to an admin-defined policy, with checkpoint-aware graceful
  semantics.

# PyTorchJob checkpoint support for graceful preemption

## Description

Branch B of the preemption implementation, Training Operator side (applies
when the preemption semantics investigation concludes checkpoint-aware
graceful preemption is required): provide checkpoint support for multi-node
PyTorchJobs so a job's progress can be captured before preemption and
restored after requeue, following the upstream Training Operator checkpoint
mechanism where applicable.

## Scope

- Enable/extend PyTorchJob checkpointing in the midstream Training Operator
  so multi-node jobs can write checkpoints on demand (before preemption).
- Support restoring a job from its latest checkpoint when it is re-admitted
  after preemption.
- Validate checkpoint and restore correctness for representative multi-node
  training jobs, with overhead consistent with the preemption benchmark.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running multi-node PyTorchJob, when a checkpoint is requested, then
  job progress is checkpointed and the job continues or stops cleanly.
- Given a PyTorchJob re-admitted after preemption, when it restarts, then it
  restores from the latest checkpoint and training resumes.
- Given representative jobs, when checkpoint/restore is exercised, then
  overhead stays within the bounds established by the preemption semantics
  benchmark.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): higher-priority workloads preempt lower-priority ones per
  admin-defined policy — this epic provides the checkpoint capability that
  graceful preemption builds on.

# Validate Kueue gang admission for PyTorchJob/RayJob at target scale

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's first open question: whether Kueue's
current gang-admission semantics (`waitForPodsReady`) actually satisfy the
all-or-nothing admission requirement for multi-node PyTorchJob and RayJob
workloads at the platform's target scale, or whether scheduler-plugin work
(e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue is required. The strategy explicitly states
that this answer changes the shape of most implementation work, so all gang
admission implementation epics are gated on this outcome.

## Scope

- Define the concrete "target scale" criteria (nodes, GPUs, concurrent mixed
  jobs) that the validation must satisfy — the strategy references target
  scale without defining it.
- Study Kueue's admission and `waitForPodsReady` semantics from source and
  documentation, including known failure modes for partial pod occupation and
  timeout behavior.
- Exercise PyTorchJob and RayJob admission through Kueue locally and on a
  shared cluster at the defined scale, observing whether GPUs are ever
  partially occupied while a job waits for remaining pods.
- Produce a decision document with one of two bounded outcomes:
  - **Outcome A**: Kueue-native semantics satisfy the all-or-nothing
    requirement; implementation proceeds as configuration/integration
    enablement.
  - **Outcome B**: Kueue-native semantics are insufficient; scheduler-plugin
    (e.g. coscheduling) work is required.

- Given a defined target-scale scenario, when a multi-node PyTorchJob and a
  RayJob are submitted under contention, then it is determined and documented
  whether any GPU is held by a partially admitted job while remaining pods
  are pending.
- Given the validation results, when a timeout or eviction of a partially
  scheduled job occurs, then the observed behavior against the
  no-partial-occupation requirement is documented with reproductions.
- A decision document records outcome A or B, the evidence, and the scale
  criteria used, so the gated implementation epics can start.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): multi-node training jobs admitted all-or-nothing — this
  investigation determines the implementation approach that will deliver it.

# Per-project GPU quota enforcement at admission time

## Description

Deliver per-project GPU quota that is enforced at admission time across
training job types (PyTorchJob and RayJob), so a project's pending and running
training workloads together cannot exceed its GPU quota. This work uses the

and is independent of the gang-admission approach decision: quota is enforced
by Kueue at admission regardless of post-admission pod scheduling semantics.

## Scope

- Define the per-project quota model for GPU resources across training job
  types, built on the Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model.
- Provide the configuration/provisioning mechanism by which each project
  receives its GPU quota and by which admins adjust it.
- Ensure both PyTorchJob and RayJob workloads in a project count against the
  same per-project GPU quota at admission time.
- Ensure jobs exceeding the project quota remain pending (not partially
  admitted) until quota is available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with a GPU quota of N, when training jobs (PyTorchJob and
  RayJob) whose combined GPU request exceeds N are submitted, then jobs are
  held pending at admission time and no GPU above the quota is occupied.
- Given two projects, when each submits training jobs, then quota consumption
  is enforced independently per project.
- Given an admin changes a project's GPU quota, when new jobs are submitted,
  then admission follows the updated quota.

  training job types (PyTorchJob, RayJob).
